s: a bookshop-café and cultural hub overlooking a quiet piazza off the Tortona design district
w: A bookshop, café, co-working space and exhibition venue in one, facing a quiet piazza just off the Tortona design district. Warm, Scandinavian-modern interiors, good coffee, and the gentle background hum of readings and small exhibitions -- a cultural anchor tucked a block from the design-week crowds rather than in the middle of them.
_facts: Located at Via Savona 101, 20144 Milano, near the Tortona design district
Combines a bookshop, café, co-working space and exhibition/events venue
Overlooks a quiet piazza just off Via Savona

s: a pandemic-era specialty coffee opening with a calm Scandi-influenced interior
w: A specialty coffee bar that opened during the pandemic years and quickly built a devoted following for precise espresso and a calm, pared-back, Scandinavian-influenced room -- a quietly distinctive note in a city more associated with the quick standing espresso. Small and focused, with locals treating it as a considered daily stop rather than a passing novelty.
_facts: Located at Via Francesco Guicciardini 3, 20129 Milano
Specialty coffee bar known for a minimalist, Scandinavian-influenced interior
Has since expanded to additional Milan locations (Via Varesina, Via Pirelli)

s: a neighbourhood covered market reborn as a social eat-in spot
w: A small covered neighbourhood market on Piazza Santa Maria del Suffragio that has grown into a place to eat as much as shop -- produce and grocery stalls alongside tables inside and on a veranda where you can buy from the stalls and sit down right there. Ordinary Milanese daily life rather than a destination market, which is exactly the point.
_facts: Located at Piazza Santa Maria del Suffragio, 20135 Milano, Porta Vittoria
Covered neighbourhood produce market with an attached eat-in area/veranda
Functions as both a working local market and a casual social spot

s: Ligurian farinata cooked in tinned copper, steps from Porta Genova station
w: A no-frills Ligurian focacceria opposite Porta Genova station, cooking farinata -- chickpea-flour flatbread -- in traditional tinned copper pans and cutting it into crisp, rosemary-scented squares eaten standing at outdoor tables. Descended from a 1994 Porta Romana original; this Via Vigevano branch has been serving the Navigli side of the tracks since 2004.
_facts: Located at Via Vigevano 45, 20144 Milano, opposite Porta Genova station
Specialises in Genovese focaccia and chickpea farinata cooked in tinned copper pans
This location opened in 2004; the original shop opened in Milan's Porta Romana area in 1994
Serves farinata and focaccia at standing outdoor tables
